Sample metadata: GEOME, GBIF, and NCBI

Source: vignettes/Sample-Metadata.Rmd
Sample-Metadata.Rmd

RiboPilot can optionally link each sample to corresponding NCBI, GBIF, or GEOME records. This information can be shown in the app, flagged where databases disagree, and used in your FASTA headers for submission to GenBank.

Database What it holds Identifier you supply
GEOME Specimen, tissue, and collecting-event records from field projects BCID, such as ark:/21547/CXu2MBIO1000.1
GBIF Museum and collection specimen records (“occurrences”) gbifID, such as 6186461308, or a Smithsonian EZID
NCBI BioSample The biological material behind GenBank and SRA (NCBI’s raw-read archive) data BioSample (SAMN29555051) or SRA accession (SRR21844202)

RiboPilot never merges values or picks one source over another. Each source keeps its own fields, and you decide which ones go into your FASTA headers. Records are not live: if the remote database changes, fetch again. Fetched data never changes how RiboPilot resolves taxonomy.

Public records only. Private GEOME or NCBI projects are not supported.

Related pages:

  • Linking records across databases: fill in the other databases from one ID.
  • NMNH voucher submissions: NMNH metadata requirements for GenBank records.
  • Metadata field reference: every export field, the column names RiboPilot recognizes, and fetch messages.

Quick start

  1. Add a column of IDs to your mapping file.
  2. Name it in new_project() (for example mapping_gbif = "Occurrence"). RiboPilot fetches the records during setup.
  3. In the app, check the Metadata column: one logo per fetched source.
  4. Click the Metadata button above a table and tick Export on the fields you want, such as gbif_lat_lon and gbif_collection_date.
  5. In Export Data, click those fields to add them to the FASTA header template, then export.

Common tasks

Task In R In the app
Link IDs at setup new_project(mapping_geome =, mapping_gbif =, mapping_ncbi =)
Add or change IDs update_sample_metadata(), or fetch_*(ids =, bcids = / gbifs = / ncbi_ids =) Click a sample’s Metadata icon, edit the ID, Fetch
Refresh records fetch_geome(), fetch_gbif(), fetch_ncbi() Refresh all in the viewer
Fill in other databases link_sources = TRUE Follow links between databases in the viewer
Pick which mapping-file columns are compared set_metadata_columns() Mapping file columns… on the Compare tab
Use fields in FASTA headers Metadata button, tick Export
Remove fetched data remove_metadata() Remove fetched data… in the viewer

Finding the identifiers

  • GEOME BCID. Open a record on geome-db.org and copy its identifier, which starts with ark:/. Use the most specific record that matches your sequenced material, usually the tissue: RiboPilot also fetches the sample, collecting event, expedition, and project above it.
  • gbifID. Open the occurrence on gbif.org and copy the number at the end of its address (https://www.gbif.org/occurrence/6186461308).
  • Smithsonian EZID. NMNH specimens can use their EZID, a permanent identifier starting with ark:/65665/, in place of a gbifID. RiboPilot finds the matching GBIF occurrence, so the specimen must be on GBIF. EZIDs are more stable than gbifIDs. Links from n2t.net or collections.nmnh.si.edu work, with or without dashes.
  • BioSample or SRA accession. Copy the BioSample accession (SAMN, SAMEA, or SAMD) from NCBI BioSample, or use the SRA accession of your reads (an SRR, ERR, or DRR run, an SRX experiment, or an SRS sample). For an SRA accession, RiboPilot finds its BioSample and also stores the run, experiment, study, platform, and library.

Full links work everywhere: RiboPilot trims them to the bare ID.

gbifIDs can change. GBIF may give an occurrence a new gbifID when its dataset is republished. If an ID stops working, RiboPilot keeps the data it fetched before and marks the fetch as failed. Look the specimen up again on gbif.org and paste the new ID.

Adding identifiers

At project setup

Add a column for any or all databases to your mapping file (see Your own project). Columns named GEOME_BCID, GBIF_ID, and BioSample (any upper or lower case) are found automatically. For other names, pass mapping_geome, mapping_gbif, and mapping_ncbi:

ID,Taxon,R1,R2,Tissue_BCID,Occurrence,SRA
Fish_01,Psenes pellucidus,Fish_01_R1.fastq.gz,Fish_01_R2.fastq.gz,ark:/21547/CXu2MBIO1000.1,,
Fish_02,Notemigonus crysoleucas,Fish_02_R1.fastq.gz,Fish_02_R2.fastq.gz,,6186461308,
Fish_03,Conger oceanicus,Fish_03_R1.fastq.gz,Fish_03_R2.fastq.gz,,,SRR21844202
RiboPilot::new_project(
  path          = "~/my_project",
  mapping_fn    = "~/my_samples.csv",
  data_path     = "~/my_reads",
  mapping_geome = "Tissue_BCID",
  mapping_gbif  = "Occurrence",
  mapping_ncbi  = "SRA"
)
  • Blank cells are fine: those samples have no link.
  • Fetching needs internet access on the machine running R or the app. Offline, pass fetch_geome = FALSE, fetch_gbif = FALSE, and fetch_ncbi = FALSE, and fetch later. Pipeline jobs never contact these databases.

new_test_project() sets up the test project with linking on. Its fetch_metadata argument turns the NCBI fetch off.

Later

In the app, click the icon in the Metadata column, type or paste the ID, and click Fetch.

In R, add_samples() and update_sample_metadata() take the same mapping_*, fetch_*, and link_sources arguments. With update_sample_metadata(), samples whose ID changed or was added are fetched again, and a blank cell removes that sample’s link and data for that source only.

To fetch again without touching the mapping file:

RiboPilot::fetch_gbif("~/my_project")                   # every gbifID
RiboPilot::fetch_gbif("~/my_project", ids = "Fish_02")  # one sample
RiboPilot::fetch_gbif("~/my_project", ids = c("Fish_01", "Fish_02"),
                      gbifs = c("2336663130", "6186461308"))  # set new IDs, then fetch
RiboPilot::fetch_ncbi("~/my_project", ids = "Fish_03", ncbi_ids = "SAMN29555051")
RiboPilot::fetch_geome("~/my_project", ids = "Fish_01",
                       bcids = "ark:/21547/CXu2MBIO1000.1")

A blank ID removes the link. When some fetches fail, the rest still finish and a warning message lists each failed sample with the reason. A failed refresh keeps the data fetched before; changing to a different ID clears the old record right away. See the fetch messages table for additional details.

NCBI allows three requests per second, or ten with a free NCBI API key. Metadata fetches use the project’s ncbi_api_key or the NCBI_API_KEY/ENTREZ_KEY environment variables.

Viewing records in the app

The Metadata column

The Taxonomy, Assemble, Annotation Review, and Export tables have a Metadata column, with one logo per source the sample has an ID for:

Icon Meaning
“+” No IDs. Click it to add one.
GEOME “G”, GBIF leaf, NCBI helix The record was fetched.
Faded logo The ID is set but not fetched yet.
Faded logo with a warning triangle The fetch failed. Hover to see why.
Orange flag The sources disagree on at least one item (see Comparing sources).

Hovering over an icon lists each source with its status, then any items in conflict.

Showing metadata in the tables

The Metadata button above each table opens the Metadata fields window. It lists every field with a value for at least one sample: your mapping-file columns, then GEOME, GBIF, and NCBI fields, with an example value and a sample count (for example 12/20). Each row has two ticks:

  • Show adds the field as a column in the Taxonomy, Assemble, Annotation Review, and Export tables.
  • Export makes the field usable in FASTA header templates and writes it to the sample summary CSV.

Mapping-file columns start with Show ticked and are always available at export. Click Save to keep your choices in the project.

The sample metadata viewer

Click a sample’s Metadata icon to open the viewer. It has a tab for each database and a Compare tab. Here you can:

  • edit an ID and click Fetch (clear the box to remove the link),
  • click Refresh all to fetch every sample again,
  • filter fields by name, copy any value, or click Export CSV to save all of a sample’s metadata.

The Sample list on the left marks samples that failed to fetch or have a conflict. On the NCBI tab, records are shown as SRA, BioSample, and BioProject cards, each linked to its NCBI page.

Comparing sources

The Compare tab puts the values from your mapping file, GEOME, GBIF, and NCBI side by side for coordinates, collection date, country, locality, voucher, collector, sex, life stage, and taxon.

Status Meaning
agree Every source with a value agrees. Coordinates agree within 0.01 degree.
conflict A real disagreement.
not checked Free text, or a value that could not be read.
single Only one source has a value.
- No source has a value.

Blanks never conflict, and placeholders such as missing or not collected count as blank. RiboPilot finds your mapping-file columns by common names. If yours differ, pick them under Mapping file columns… at the bottom of the Compare tab, or in R:

RiboPilot::set_metadata_columns("~/my_project", country = "Country_Name",
                                coordinates = c("Lat_DD", "Long_DD"))
RiboPilot::set_metadata_columns("~/my_project", country = NA)  # back to automatic
RiboPilot::set_metadata_columns("~/my_project", sex = "")      # do not compare sex

Using metadata fields at export

A fetched value reaches your FASTA headers only after you tick Export for it in the Metadata button (see Showing metadata in the tables). Each source offers GenBank-ready fields, already formatted as GenBank source modifiers: the [name=value] tags in a FASTA header, such as [lat_lon=17.48 S 149.90 W]. The other fields are the raw values from each record. See GenBank submission for header templates and the modifiers GenBank requires.

In the Export Data window, the Available metadata panel lists every field you can use. Click one to insert it into the FASTA header box. A GenBank-ready field inserts the whole modifier, such as [lat_lon={gbif_lat_lon}]. Choose fields next to a source opens the Metadata fields window so you can enable more fields for export.

A template that takes every specimen value from GBIF:

{seqid} [organism={organism}] [moltype=genomic DNA] [lat_lon={gbif_lat_lon}] [collection_date={gbif_collection_date}] [geo_loc_name={gbif_geo_loc_name}] [specimen_voucher={gbif_specimen_voucher}] {organism} {rrna_definition}
  • Take a record’s values from one source where you can. Mixing sources can combine coordinates and dates from different collecting events. If you cite a BioSample with [BioSample=], GenBank expects the header values to agree with it.
  • Empty values are left out. A modifier with no value for a sample is dropped from that sample’s header instead of written empty, which GenBank rejects. The check under each header box names the records with empty modifiers, and warns when the same modifier appears twice. GenBank requires collection_date and geo_loc_name, so fill them in or use a missing-value term such as missing (see Required source modifiers).
  • Check GBIF values. GBIF’s country is its own English name (United States of America, where GenBank expects USA), and GBIF may have adjusted or generalized coordinates. See the GBIF notes.
  • Your mapping file wins on a name clash. If your mapping file has a column with the same name as a ticked field (for example geome_lat_lon), its value is used in headers and the summary.

When you click Export, RiboPilot checks the items your templates use. If any sample in the export group has a conflict on one of them, the Sample metadata disagrees warning lists each sample, item, and value. Click Export anyway or Cancel.

NMNH specimens need two extra modifiers; see NMNH voucher submissions.

Removing fetched data

Remove fetched data… under the sample list in the viewer, or remove_metadata(), deletes fetched records for one sample or all:

RiboPilot::remove_metadata("~/my_project")                    # everything fetched
RiboPilot::remove_metadata("~/my_project", sources = "GBIF")  # one source
RiboPilot::remove_metadata("~/my_project", sources = c("GEOME", "GBIF"),
                           ids = "Fish_02")

This removes the stored records, their fetch status, and IDs that linking filled in. Your mapping-file columns, the IDs you supplied, and your field ticks are kept, so Refresh all or fetch_*() brings the data back.
